cells.tense: The spark is here in the room and one person is at the table with it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that is trying to begin. Say out loud what it would need first. One plain sentence, no shape it has to fit.
cells.core:
Something has caught fire in you and hasn't picked a direction yet. You can hold that and stay in the room. The whole thing sits in front of you, unshaped, and you keep looking at it without forcing an answer. Most people either put the fire out early or decide by Tuesday that it is something else entirely.

What bends this is that a spark doesn't need to stay unspoken. So pick one thing that is trying to begin and say what it would need first. One plain sentence, out loud, to no one in particular. After that, go do the next ordinary thing you were going to do anyway.

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that has not arrived yet and cannot be written in from here.
cells.ask: Take one beginning and name its very first step. Write that step on paper. Do it today, rough, before the picture feels sorted.
cells.core:
You are seeing the whole shape too far ahead. Nothing has actually begun yet and there is already a plan for how to explain it — running versions, checking whether they hold, getting ready for the part where someone asks what it is. Your ability to see the pattern is real. What it costs is the beginning itself: a spark that only wanted to catch must now survive being understood first.

So take one of these openings and name its first step. Write it on paper. Do that step today, rough, before the picture feels sorted. When the whole is clearer than the piece, the piece stops being available.

cells.tense: Things keep starting around you and you keep watching them without stepping in.
cells.ask: Show one unfinished thing to someone who will not sort it for you. Say what is there and stop. Let the saying be the whole act.
cells.core:
Something near you wants to begin and you can see the whole of it. You clock the moment, the spark, the shape, then let it pass without firing. Not because it isn't worth moving on. Because you have gotten used to the blur, and the blur asks nothing of anybody. Sitting still with a clear view is the safest place in the room.

More watching is not what this needs. Pick one unfinished thing and show it to someone who will not tidy it for you. Say what is there. Stop before the conclusions. The whole of the act is saying it and leaving it be.

cells.tense: Beginnings keep happening around you and you keep calling them timing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have already started and have been calling circumstance. Say 'I began this' out loud. Then leave it.
cells.core:
You talk about openings arriving on you as though you had nothing to do with them. Look at the last stretch of months: doors keep appearing because you keep leaning toward them, and afterward you describe it as the moment, the timing, the way it went. You are doing the starting. What's absent is owning that part in plain speech.

That gap changes how the whole pattern reads — you can see it from outside and still not count the piece that is you. So name one thing you began and have been calling circumstance. Say 'I began this' out loud, nobody else in the room. Then leave it alone.
